author: t.wambsgans
content:
So either we
1) pre-propagate + pre-aggregate the top layer (a bit of difficulty, but maybe doable?) -> everything (signature size and xmss aggregation time) gets 2x better.
or 2) we go back to a single XMSS layer (bad for DVT with DKG):
2a) if we want small signature (1200 bytes): **33% faster xmss aggregation**
2b) if we are fine to be above 1200 bytes (as it's today), then roughly **50% faster xmss aggregation**

author: t.wambsgans
content: we could. It would mean let validators specify either 1 or 2 sub-trees at registration. It would work. The first issue I see is that there is an incentive to always go with 2 (because much faster keygen), and it's the one that is the hardest to handle for Ethereum. So it means we would need some way to disincentives it (x% less reward, idk). And second issue: it adds a bit of complexity. But still, I think it may be a viable solution.
